original_question: For general initial data in general relativity, either prove the Penrose inequality relating apparent-horizon area and total mass, or give a counterexample showing that the inequality fails in the general case.
target_in_paper: Section 3.2, Problem P3: "Find a proof of the Penrose inequality or present a counterexample in the general case," read together with Penrose's original formulation RP13 and Bartnik's shorthand restatement RB7.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the Penrose inequality as the target, keeps the paper's prove-or-counterexample framing, and correctly describes the issue as a relation between horizon area and total mass in classical general relativity. It also correctly aims at the unresolved general case rather than the already proved Riemannian/time-symmetric case alone.
missing_details: The nearest official formulation in this paper is Section 3.2, Problem P3, not a generic request about all Penrose-type inequalities.
The relevant mass is specifically the ADM mass of the initial hypersurface, not an unspecified "total mass."

The relevant geometric object is described in Section 3.2 as a marginally (outer) future-trapped surface (the apparent horizon); the paper's later Penrose formulation RP13 uses a trapped surface as part of the boundary data.
RP13 explicitly assumes the dominant energy condition, which your draft omits.
RP13 also specifies the geometric setup: a compact spacelike hypersurface S whose boundary consists of a cut C of future null infinity together with a trapped surface (the black-hole horizon).

The paper distinguishes the already proved Riemannian version from the still-open general Lorentzian case; a paper-faithful rewrite should make clear that the open problem is the general/Lorentzian case.

Section 3.2 does not write an explicit numerical formula; it only states that there should be a lower bound on ADM mass in terms of the horizon/trapped-surface area. A faithful rewrite should not insert a sharper formula not stated there.
The paper notes that even in spherical symmetry only a weaker version using energy rather than mass is known; this helps specify what the unresolved "general case" excludes.

Your phrase "for general initial data" is slightly broader than the paper's main target, since Section 3.2 separately remarks that generalizing to non-time-symmetric initial data is itself an additional direction of interest.

Algebraic items such as ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency are not relevant here; the omitted stand-alone hypotheses are geometric and relativistic instead (asymptotic flatness, ADM mass, trapped/apparent horizon, boundary at null infinity, and energy condition).
refined_question: Under the dominant energy condition, prove or disprove the Penrose inequality in the general Lorentzian setting of classical general relativity: for asymptotically flat initial data with ADM mass whose initial hypersurface contains a marginally (outer) future-trapped surface (apparent horizon), more explicitly a compact spacelike hypersurface S whose boundary consists of a cut C of future null infinity together with a trapped surface, must the ADM mass satisfy the Penrose lower bound determined by the area of the trapped/horizon boundary component, or can one construct a counterexample?
justification: The draft is closest to Problem P3 in Section 3.2 because that is the paper's own prove-or-counterexample formulation for the Penrose inequality "in the general case." The surrounding discussion there identifies the inequality as one involving the area of a marginally (outer) future-trapped surface (apparent horizon) and the ADM mass of the initial hypersurface, and it stresses that the Riemannian version is proved while the Lorentzian case remains open. Penrose's original problem RP13 later supplies the sharper hypotheses missing from the brief statement in Section 3.2: compact spacelike hypersurface, boundary made of a cut of future null infinity plus a trapped surface, and the dominant energy condition. RB7 is only the shorter Bartnik restatement, so P3 plus RP13 is the most faithful sharpening of your draft.
